newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise, seen rising further.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise, seen rising further.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.09 percent on Wednesday after Janez Podobnik was elected as parliamentary president and traders said the uptrend was likely to continue over the next two weeks.

"The election of Podobnik is good news, which could mean that the two blocs reached some agreement leading to Drnovsek remaining prime minister" Goran Brankovic, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka said.

Shares eased after Slovenia's inconclusive general election on November 10, which gave neither left nor right a clear mandate to run the country, and traders held their breath ahead of the formation of a new government.
* The 10-share SBI index rose 12.72 points to 1,180.0.
* Drug maker Lek A issue was the most actively traded, rising 3.95 percent to 19,750 tolars on volume of 5,775 shares.
* Overall 12 shares rose and six fell, while seven were untraded. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
